title: [DocDB] Index inconsistency in system catalog tablet
body:
Jira Link: [DB-516](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-516)
### Description

Full details of this issue including links to prior discussions are available for internal users in Zendesk ticket 2908.

Following an upgrade from Yugabyte DB version 2.4.4 to version 2.8.3, backups of some of the customer's databases began failing at the database schema export step. Backups created prior to the upgrade were successful. Backups following the upgrade failed.

The corresponding errors from the Platform logs are:

```
2022-03-11 06:33:25,601 [DEBUG] from ShellProcessHandler in TaskPool-MultiTableBackup(4012307b-f75a-410e-a2a0-1ef76bded847)-0 - ysql_dump: [archiver (db)] query failed: ERROR:  Query error: ybctid DocKey([], ["@{\x1e\xb6\x04\x10J\xd4\xa9\xb9\x8b\x1e/\x14e\xd4"]) not found in indexed table
2022-03-11 06:33:25,601 [DEBUG] from ShellProcessHandler in TaskPool-MultiTableBackup(4012307b-f75a-410e-a2a0-1ef76bded847)-0 - ysql_dump: [archiver (db)] query was: SELECT c.tableoid, c.oid, c.relname, (SELECT pg_catalog.array_agg(acl ORDER BY row_n) FROM (SELECT acl, row_n FROM pg_catalog.unnest(coalesce(c.relacl,pg_catalog.acldefault(CASE WHEN c.relkind = 'S' THEN 's' ELSE 'r' END::"char",c.relowner))) WITH ORDINALITY AS perm(acl,row_n) WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM pg_catalog.unnest(coalesce(pip.initprivs,pg_catalog.acldefault(CASE WHEN c.relkind = 'S' THEN 's' ELSE 'r' END::"char",c.relowner))) AS init(init_acl) WHERE acl = init_acl)) as foo) AS relacl, (SELECT pg_catalog.array_agg(acl ORDER BY row_n) FROM (SELECT acl, row_n FROM pg_catalog.unnest(coalesce(pip.initprivs,pg_catalog.acldefault(CASE WHEN c.relkind = 'S' THEN 's' ELSE 'r' END::"char",c.relowner))) WITH ORDINALITY AS initp(acl,row_n) WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM pg_catalog.unnest(coalesce(c.relacl,pg_catalog.acldefault(CASE WHEN c.relkind = 'S' THEN 's' ELSE 'r' END::"char",c.relowner))) AS permp(orig_acl) WHERE acl = orig_acl)) as foo) as rrelacl, NULL AS initrelacl, NULL as initrrelacl, c.relkind, c.relnamespace, (SELECT rolname FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles WHERE oid = c.relowner) AS rolname, c.relchecks, c.relhastriggers, c.relhasindex, c.relhasrules, c.relhasoids, c.relrowsecurity, c.relforcerowsecurity, c.relfrozenxid, c.relminmxid, tc.oid AS toid, tc.relfrozenxid AS tfrozenxid, tc.relminmxid AS tminmxid, c.relpersistence, c.relispopulated, c.relreplident, c.relpages, CASE WHEN c.reloftype <> 0 THEN c.reloftype::pg_catalog.regtype ELSE NULL END AS reloftype, d.refobjid AS owning_tab, d.refobjsubid AS owning_col, (SELECT spcname FROM pg_tablespace t WHERE t.oid = c.reltablespace) AS reltablespace, array_remove(array_remove(c.reloptions,'check_option=local'),'check_option=cascaded') AS reloptions, CASE WHEN 'check_option=local' = ANY (c.reloptions) THEN 'LOCAL'::text WHEN 'check_option=cascaded' = ANY (c.reloptions) THEN 'CASCADED'::text ELSE NULL END AS checkoption, tc.reloptions AS toast_reloptions, c.relkind = 'S' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_depend WHERE classid = 'pg_class'::regclass AND objid = c.oid AND objsubid = 0 AND refclassid = 'pg_class'::regclass AND deptype = 'i') AS is_identity_sequence, EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_attribute at LEFT JOIN pg_init_privs pip ON (c.oid = pip.objoid AND pip.classoid = 'pg_class'::regclass AND pip.objsubid = at.attnum)WHERE at.attrelid = c.oid AND ((SELECT pg_catalog.array_agg(acl ORDER BY row_n) FROM (SELECT acl, row_n FROM pg_catalog.unnest(coalesce(at.attacl,pg_catalog.acldefault('c',c.relowner))) WITH ORDINALITY AS perm(acl,row_n) WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM pg_catalog.unnest(coalesce(pip.initprivs,pg_catalog.acldefault('c',c.relowner))) AS init(init_acl) WHERE acl = init_acl)) as foo) IS NOT NULL OR (SELECT pg_catalog.array_agg(acl ORDER BY row_n) FROM (SELECT acl, row_n FROM pg_catalog.unnest(coalesce(pip.initprivs,pg_catalog.acldefault('c',c.relowner))) WITH ORDINALITY AS initp(acl,row_n) WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM pg_catalog.unnest(coalesce(at.attacl,pg_catalog.acldefault('c',c.relowner))) AS permp(orig_acl) WHERE acl = orig_acl)) as foo) IS NOT NULL OR NULL IS NOT NULL OR NULL IS NOT NULL))AS changed_acl, pg_get_partkeydef(c.oid) AS partkeydef, c.relispartition AS ispartition, pg_get_expr(c.relpartbound, c.oid) AS partbound FROM pg_class c LEFT JOIN pg_depend d ON (c.relkind = 'S' AND d.classid = c.tableoid AND d.objid = c.oid AND d.objsubid = 0 AND d.refclassid = c.tableoid AND d.deptype IN ('a', 'i')) LEFT JOIN pg_class tc ON (c.reltoastrelid = tc.oid) LEFT JOIN pg_init_privs pip ON (c.oid = pip.objoid AND pip.classoid = 'pg_class'::regclass AND pip.objsubid = 0) WHERE c.relkind in ('r', 'S', 'v', 'c', 'm', 'f', 'p') ORDER BY c.oid
```

These messages indicates that we performed an Index scan but when we attempted to retrieve the key recorded in the index from the main table, the key was not found. The reported DocKey `DocKey([], ["@{\x1e\xb6\x04\x10J\xd4\xa9\xb9\x8b\x1e/\x14e\xd4"])` is identical every time.

The query that is failing is responsible for generating the list of tables in the database.

This issue affects the system catalog and corresponding tablet `00000000000000000000000000000000`.

After extensive troubleshooting, we managed to work around the problem by disabling the indexes on the `pg_depend` table for affected databases, e.g.:

```
\c <database_name>
SET yb_non_ddl_txn_for_sys_tables_allowed=on;
UPDATE pg_index SET indisvalid=false WHERE indrelid='pg_depend'::regclass;
SET yb_non_ddl_txn_for_sys_tables_allowed=off;
```

There are four databases on this system that are affected by this issue. Fortunately, one of the databases is the built-in `yugabyte` database which the customer does not use, so if we need to do some testing in the affected environment, we should be able to do so without impacting their production workload.

I believe there are three possible causes for this issue:
1. Extraneous data was somehow added to the index
2. Required data was somehow removed from the main table
3. The index and main table are both correct but some intermediary such as a Bloom filter is returning incorrect results. As an example, #6435 is an (unrelated) issue that produced similar symptoms.

Since there is a workaround in place and the customer is getting backups again, this issue is no longer an emergency but we do need to find a way to determine what is wrong with the system catalog and repair it.

For next steps, I am considering flushing the system catalog on the customer's system using `yb-admin compact_sys_catalog` and then tarring the whole thing up and making it available for direct examination by the dev team.

Is this a reasonable plan? Are there any potential pitfalls?
